title: Reproducibility Report for SC25 Paper X-MoE: Enabling Scalable Training for Emerging Mixture-of-Experts Architectures on HPC Platforms
problem: Reproducibility of HPC and AI systems research requires independent evaluation of published artifacts and methodologies.
motivation: SC25 Reproducibility Initiative aims to validate research claims through artifact evaluation, ensuring scientific integrity and enabling community replication.
method: To verify the X-MoE paper's results, researchers downloaded and ran the authors' code on HPC systems (supercomputers), testing how efficiently mixture-of-experts training—a technique that routes different data to multiple specialized neural network sub-components—scales as computing power increases. They repeated the original experiments and measured whether they achieved the same performance improvements reported in the paper. This independent verification was part of the SC25 Supercomputing Conference's official Reproducibility Committee review process.
key_novelty: This report independently confirms that X-MoE's published results for training mixture-of-experts models (networks that route data to multiple specialized sub-components) on supercomputers are reproducible by following the authors' methodology.
contributions: Validation of X-MoE scalable training methodology
Assessment of artifact quality and documentation
limitations: Report focuses on artifact evaluation methodology rather than technical contributions; specific findings depend on X-MoE paper being evaluated.
